objections.claim: Every CA-3 subtype has an executable product/slice-authority route in the necessary-not-sufficient admission rule.
objections.evidence: Clause 4 names DR-108 for keychain access but groups the remaining CA-3 effects under 'their existing slice authorities.' The measured BLK-2 contains four materially different effects: keychain, local socket/named pipe, out-of-root path access, and privileged platform facilities. The old join records IPC as reserved and absent from the measured slice, out-of-root access as having no vocabulary row, and privileged facilities as unnamed or undecidable. No row or owner is named in this subject for those three effects. Clause 5 then routes BLK-2 to 'the per-subtype authorities in clause 4,' which do not exist in the text for three of four subtypes. Necessary-not-sufficient plus fail-closed prevents silent admission, but it does not tell a successor which authority can make those cases eligible.
objections.proposedFix: Enumerate all four CA-3 subtypes. Preserve DR-108 for keychain; name the D-002/product authority and any existing reserved-extension owner for IPC/socket, out-of-root access, and privileged facilities, or explicitly record each as UNOWNED with a required D-000 owner-assignment decision. State that the host-effect contract can define mechanics only after the named product/slice authority admits that subtype.
